questions.q:
(a) State what is meant by a hydrocarbon. [1]
(b) State two uses of ethanol. [2]
ms: (a) a compound containing hydrogen and carbon only
questions.model:
(a) A hydrocarbon is a compound that contains hydrogen and carbon only.
(b) Ethanol is used as a solvent and as a fuel.
questions.tip: 'Only' is essential in the hydrocarbon definition — ethanol contains oxygen, so it is not a hydrocarbon.

questions.q:
Petroleum is separated into fractions by fractional distillation. Name the fraction used for:
(a) making roads [1]
(b) fuel for cars [1]
(c) fuel for diesel engines. [1]
questions.tip: Learn the five fractions with their uses as pairs: refinery gas, gasoline, naphtha, diesel oil, bitumen.

questions.q:
Three compounds are shown by their structural formulae.
A: CH₃CH₂CH₃
B: CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃
C: CH₃CH₂OH
(a) Name compounds A, B and C. [3]
(b) Which compound is unsaturated? Give a reason. [1]
ms: (b) B, because it has a C=C double bond
questions.model:
(a) A is propane, B is but-1-ene and C is ethanol.
(b) B is unsaturated because it contains a carbon–carbon double bond.
questions.tip: Number the double bond from the nearer end: CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃ is but-1-ene, not but-3-ene.

questions.q:
Butane, C₄H₁₀, is used as a camping gas fuel.
(a) Write the balanced symbol equation for the complete combustion of butane. [2]
(b) In a tent with poor ventilation, incomplete combustion of butane can occur. Name a harmful gas produced and state why it is harmful. [2]
questions.model:
(a) 2C₄H₁₀ + 13O₂ → 8CO₂ + 10H₂O
(b) Carbon monoxide, which is a toxic gas.
questions.tip: Balance C, then H, then O last; double everything if you end up with a half.

questions.q:
Decane, C₁₀H₂₂, can be cracked to form octane and ethene.
(a) State the conditions needed for cracking. [2]
(b) Write the balanced symbol equation for this cracking reaction. [1]
(c) Suggest why oil companies crack large alkane molecules. [1]
(d) Ethene reacts with bromine. Write the equation for this reaction and explain why it is called an addition reaction. [2]
ms: (c) to make smaller, more useful molecules (e.g. for petrol) because demand for them is greater than supply / to make alkenes (ethene) for polymers
(d) two molecules join to form a single product (the double bond opens)
questions.model:
(a) A high temperature and a catalyst.
(b) C₁₀H₂₂ → C₈H₁₈ + C₂H₄
(c) There is more demand for the smaller molecules, such as petrol, than is supplied by fractional distillation, and cracking also makes alkenes such as ethene for making polymers.
(d) C₂H₄ + Br₂ → C₂H₄Br₂. The C=C double bond opens and the bromine atoms add on, so two molecules join to form only one product.
questions.tip: Cracking always gives a shorter alkane plus an alkene (or hydrogen): check that C and H both balance.

questions.q:
(a) Describe how poly(ethene) is formed from ethene. [2]
(b) Chloroethene, CH₂=CHCl, forms an addition polymer. Draw or write the repeat unit of this polymer. [1]
(c) Describe two differences between addition polymerisation and condensation polymerisation. [2]
(d) Nylon is a condensation polymer. State the type of polymer it is. [1]
ms: (a) many ethene molecules / monomers join together (to form a long chain)
(a) the C=C double bond breaks / opens (addition polymerisation)
(c) condensation also produces a small molecule (such as water); addition gives only the polymer
(c) addition monomers contain C=C double bonds; condensation usually uses two different monomers (with two reactive groups each)
questions.model:
(a) Many ethene monomers join together to form a long chain: the C=C double bond in each ethene molecule opens and the molecules bond to each other. This is addition polymerisation.
(b) –[CH₂–CHCl]– with bonds extending out of each side.
(c) In addition polymerisation the polymer is the only product, but in condensation polymerisation a small molecule such as water is also formed. Addition monomers contain a C=C double bond, whereas condensation polymers such as nylon are usually made from two different monomers.
(d) Nylon is a polyamide.
questions.tip: For an addition repeat unit, the C=C becomes C–C and both end bonds must stick out of the brackets.
